reasons.action: The request "swap them both" only changes who occupies the two roles; it names no new behaviour, performance or movement. Changing which figure performs the existing action does not itself alter the action, so the edit-source clip's observed action (driving a nail, raising the hammer, turning to camera) continues to govern.
reasons.medium: The host rendering permission is preserve and the medium owner is pinned to the reference. The edit source is live-action cinematic footage and the swap request supplies no style phrase, treatment or target rendering, so the medium remains reference-governed.
reasons.wardrobe: No clothing or accessory change is requested. The replacement portraits provide identity wardrobe (yellow raincoat, blue coat, plaid flannel, grey apron) as observed reference values, and the clip's observed garments for remaining figures are likewise reference-supplied; the studio plates do not authorize any further wardrobe substitution.
reasons.lighting: Nothing is asked about the light, a source, its direction or its visible quality. The portraits' even studio lighting is identity-plate presentation and must not replace the clip's world, so the workshop's bright natural daylight from the multi-paned windows remains reference-governed.
reasons.framing: No camera composition, shot scale, viewpoint or movement is requested; the 16:9 canvas and the act of swapping figures are not framing instructions. The edit source's medium-wide shot with the camera tightening on the subject therefore remains reference-governed.
reasons.palette: No colour, saturation or tonal-contrast grade is requested. Incidental colours in the portraits (yellow raincoat, blue coat) and the grey studio backdrops do not recolor or regrade the scene, so the clip's live-action cinematic palette remains reference-governed.
